tool: W1-F7-WATER-r4 critic — every number I derived myself, with the command that produced it
rule: Nothing here is inherited from the r4 status file, the r3 verdict or my brief. Each block names how it was produced. Where I re-derived a figure the build also published and it agreed, I say CONFIRMED and give my own value.

A_the_shoreline_census_re_derived_in_my_.how: scratch script written by me against game/src/world/field.js's WorldField, reproducing province.js:1531-1562's cell arithmetic from the source I read this turn. It does NOT import tools/visual/f7-r4-shoreline-census.mjs.
A_the_shoreline_census_re_derived_in_my_.ruling: CONFIRMED to the digit, independently. The Deep Marshes is not shoreless. The two seas are where the depth signal is dead.

B_what_the_shipped_band_actually_covers.how: my own script over the same WorldField. esDepthM = clamp((q-0.43)/0.57,0,1)*1.35 is the exact inverse of province.js's q, so a wet corner's esDepthM IS its depth in metres. esBandM = 1 - smoothstep(0, band, esDepthM), evaluated per wet corner inside the 120 m box.
B_what_the_shipped_band_actually_covers.why_it_matters: RI-VIS04 §9's MIN BAR component is a SHORELINE depth fade. A term that is non-zero over most of the water body is not one.
B_what_the_shipped_band_actually_covers.ruling: At the shipped 1.20 m the term is non-zero over 65.1% of the Deep Marshes water in frame and over 98.6% of the Western Rootlands water in frame. That is not a shoreline fade; it is a depth-driven transparency multiplier over the whole water body. It is ONE cause for BOTH of the round's symptoms: a fade applied nearly everywhere has almost no edge (no gradient), and it lowers alpha nearly everywhere (the darkening).

C_the_water_presence_control.how: offline, on the BUILD's OWN banked frames, my own script. Every artifact dir carries a `--water-hidden` frame — the same pose with all 93 water meshes hidden — and nobody scored it. Over the pinned mask rebuilt exactly as maskFrom(PIN, hidden, thr): presence = (L[arm] - L[hidden]) / (L[prefix] - L[hidden]). 1.00 = round 2's water. 0.00 = no water at all.
C_the_water_presence_control.why_it_matters: The build states the disagreement a critic must settle as 'the starting region's water reads as more absent' versus 'the mechanism is now correct'. This turns the first half into a number, and it is threshold-independent where gradient_width_px is not.
C_the_water_presence_control.the_decomposition_the_round_had_the_arms: At edge-b135 the depth COLOUR alone (`no-shorefade`, uWaterShoreFade = 0) leaves 89.4% of the water. Round 3's k-gated ALPHA fade takes it to 59.5%. Round 4's band takes it to 41.2%. So the darkening is 10.6 points of colour and 48.2 points of ALPHA — it is the shoreline alpha term, not the depth colour, and the build's defence that 'the colour half is deliberately untouched' does not reach it.

D_the_band_sweep_the_round_never_ran.how: my own run, `corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F7-WATER-r4-critic/critic-sweep.mjs` (a copy of the build's instrument whose ONLY change is four extra uniform arms at 0.10/0.20/0.30/0.45 m), `--site vista-deep-marshes --poses edge-b135 --thresholds 6,10`. Output: `bandsweep-b135/sweep.json`.
D_the_band_sweep_the_round_never_ran.why_it_matters: The build's sweep covered 0.60 / 1.20 / 1.35 and concluded 'no band constant rescues it — so it is not a tuning problem'. Every one of those sits above the median wet-corner depth in frame (block B), i.e. entirely inside the broad regime.
D_the_band_sweep_the_round_never_ran.ruling: **THE WIDTH IS FLAT AT 34 px FROM 0.10 m TO 1.20 m AND THE DARKENING IS MONOTONIC IN THE CONSTANT.** At this pose the constant buys nothing but absence. The shipped 1.20 m is DOMINATED by 0.10 m on the build's own instrument: identical width, ten percentage points more water. 'It is not a tuning problem' is false as stated — what is true is narrower and more interesting: the width is a STEP function of whether a band exists at all, not a function of its size.
D_the_band_sweep_the_round_never_ran.what_i_did_NOT_establish: I ran this at edge-b135 only. The build's failing pose is edge-b225, where it measured 0.60 / 1.20 / 1.35 all reading 1 px and where I did NOT test 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.30. So I have NOT shown that a small band rescues edge-b225, and nobody should read that into this table.

E1_threshold_6_is_not_stable_and_the_rou.how: read off the build's own banked sweep.json files. `prefix` IS the mask arm: its own-mask delta is the instrument re-measuring an unchanged shader through the arms loop.
E1_threshold_6_is_not_stable_and_the_rou.ruling: The published replicate is taken PIN -> PIN2 back to back; the arms are measured across shader round-trips. So the band understates the instability by 10x to 50x. The build's claim that 'thresholds 6 and 10 are stable to about 1-2%' is falsified by rows inside its own artifacts. **Threshold 10 is the only stable threshold on this scene, and every headline row in the status file is a threshold-6 row.**

E2_own_mask_delta_tracks_CAPTURE_ORDINAL.how: read off the build's own banked sweep.json files, arm order = capture order.
E2_own_mask_delta_tracks_CAPTURE_ORDINAL.the_falsifier: `no-shorefade` sets uWaterShoreFade = 0. Its water alpha is IDENTICAL to the pin arm's, so of every arm it should move the mask LEAST. It moves it MOST (+35.67% at thr10, +75.67% at thr6) — and it is captured last. In my own eight-arm run the delta rises monotonically across all eight ordinals including between two bands 0.10 m apart.
E2_own_mask_delta_tracks_CAPTURE_ORDINAL.ruling: **`own_mask_delta_pct` in this round is drift accumulating with capture order, not an arm choosing its own pixels.** HAZARDS §25 remains true as a hazard on the r3 critic's original single-frame-pair evidence (a FresnelDelta sign flip and a spurious ShoreDelta pass). Round 4's '+23.24% against a replicate band of -1.13%, a measured 20x effect' does NOT establish it and should not be quoted as the band for §25.
E2_own_mask_delta_tracks_CAPTURE_ORDINAL.what_would_settle_it: One run at the same pose with the arm order REVERSED (fixed, no-shorefade, r3, prefix). If prefix at the last ordinal reads a large positive delta, it is ordinal. I launched exactly that run and killed it by PID when `node tools/contention.mjs` went to 4.53 per core against a ceiling of 4.0. It is owed.

E3_the_widths_at_the_only_stable_thresho.ruling: At the stable threshold: one large gain (b135), NO CHANGE at b045, and two 1-px moves the wrong way. The status file's second 'improvement', `edge-b045` 15 -> 17, exists only at threshold 6 — where that pose's mask arm drifts +61.75%. At threshold 10 that pose reads 20 / 20 / 20. The acceptance (>= 12 at the worst pose) fails either way, at 1.

E4_shore_raw_does_not_reproduce_and_the_.how: same pose, same tool, two processes: the build's dm-edge2 and my bandsweep-b135.
E4_shore_raw_does_not_reproduce_and_the_.ruling: The build names as an overturn condition 'any evidence that the 1 -> 34 result is an artefact of the morphological closing'. **It does not fire, and the opposite is true.** The CLOSED width reproduces across processes on every arm; `shore_raw` — the figure the build offers as the honest r3-comparable one — moved 1 -> 33 on an UNCHANGED arm between two runs, which is the size of the entire headline effect. The raw distance transform is the unreliable half.

E5_the_frame_time_figures_are_not_in_the.how: `dm-perf/sweep.json` carries `perf: {}`; grep for 3703 or 5605 across the whole W1-F7-WATER-r4 artifact tree returns nothing.
E5_the_frame_time_figures_are_not_in_the.ruling: The conclusion — no frame-time reading is obtainable on this box — is independently supported and I confirm it from source: `game/src/engine.js:9379-9381` declares `renderCpuMs` in `_unmeasurable`, in its own words, 'Tier-H. This container is SwiftShader; a wall-clock render time here is a fact about the software rasteriser, not the game'. But the specific numbers the status publishes to prove it are NOT verifiable from the artifacts. This is HAZARDS §18's shape: a report that writes only at the end loses everything when the run dies.

F_what_i_re_derived_and_CONFIRMED.depthWrite: CONFIRMED false for the whole water family, at source — `game/src/render/visual-foundation.js:689`, `depthWrite: options.depthWrite ?? family!=='water'` — and on all four live materials in the build's banked `gpu_state_before`. The r3 status file's claim that round 3 'lowered alpha on a material with depthWrite on' is corrected.
F_what_i_re_derived_and_CONFIRMED.the_transparency_sort: CONFIRMED by re-doing the arithmetic on the banked luma. strip 44.362 -> 42.517 = -1.845 (-4.16%); plane_only 66.945 -> 44.714 = -22.231 (-33.21%); land 76.598 -> 76.030 = -0.568 (-0.74%), inside the 1.18% pin replicate. The wet-bank strip moves 8.0x less, as a fraction, than the water it sits on. **The strongest recorded argument against keeping does not fire.**
F_what_i_re_derived_and_CONFIRMED.the_stale_HUD_region_label: CONFIRMED, and visually at 4 of 4 Deep Marshes poses. The build's banked `stand_verification` reads teleport_offset_m 0.00, running-field regionAt = `deep-marshes` at both the deck point and the player, hud_region_name 'The Deep Marshes'. My own offline WorldField returns `deep-marshes` at (3123.5, 3715). The label DRAWN in the frame reads `western-rootlands` in every one of edge-b045/b135/b225/b315. **The field is right and the drawn label is stale.** Three rounds of F7 evidence have been doubted over it; that doubt is withdrawn.
F_what_i_re_derived_and_CONFIRMED.the_blind_census: Re-derived with my own commands. `grep -rl 'blind_pair: yes' corpus/ --include=*.md | wc -l` = 106 FILES; restricted to reference items, `| grep -E '/RI-[^/]*\.md$' | wc -l` = **81**. `grep -rEn '"blind_status" *: *"run"' corpus/90-verdicts/` = **0**. Enumerating every wave-1 verdict's `blind_comparisons[].status`, the only `done` rows are the ten in `W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1/r2`. **81 reference items declare a blind pair; Protocol A is the entire blind-judgement history of this project.** The build's 106/3 is the file count and three false positives; both of us are describing the same fact.
F_what_i_re_derived_and_CONFIRMED.NormalEnergy_and_the_dither_stipple: CONFIRMED. Every NormalEnergy row I read is well over the 0.035 band. And the heavy dotted stipple is plainly the dominant texture of our water at every pose I opened, in both regions, on every arm — a fourth round in which somebody names it and nobody writes its reference item. I did not write it either.

G_an_internal_contradiction_in_the_statu.what: `every_number_the_instruments_emitted.gradient_width_px...pose_set_completeness` says 'Deep Marshes 4 of 4 declared bearings (M12a clause 1 satisfied)'. `method_deviations[2]` says 'only 3 valid poses in the Deep Marshes and 1 in the Western Rootlands. M12a clause 1 is therefore not satisfied in EITHER region and every band in this file fails closed.'
G_an_internal_contradiction_in_the_statu.ruling: On the artifacts the first is right: all four Deep Marshes bearings have non-void rows with `water_edge_verified.on_screen` true, taken through the corrected protocol (`dm-b045/`, `dm-edge2/`, `dm-b225/`, `dm-b315/`). M12a clause 1 IS satisfied in the Deep Marshes and is NOT satisfied in the Western Rootlands (1 of 4). It does not change any outcome — the worst pose fails the acceptance in both readings — but a critic reading `method_deviations` alone would void the round's whole pose set.

H_carried_forward_per_ARBITRATION_S64.what: The build's banked `gpu_state_before` at the Deep Marshes stand reports 46 wet-bank strips and exactly one distinct strip mesh: `water:shoreline:eastern-rootlands`. There is no `water:shoreline:deep-marshes` mesh anywhere in the resident scene, against 47 waterline cells within 120 m of that stand.
H_carried_forward_per_ARBITRATION_S64.ruling: Confirmed from the artifact. It is `game/src/world/province.js`'s file, not F7's, and it is claimed by another piece. Carried as a candidate defect and NOT absorbed.
